sourceFitAssessment.accuracyGuardrails: Keep events/all people and events/non-events as separate denominators. The same count example illustrates odds versus risk; do not read an odds ratio as a risk ratio or clinical effect without context.
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: The same two painted 100-person grids supply 40/60 and 20/80 response/nonresponse counts. Solid full-group and dashed nonresponse frames contain the exact intended people; the visual explicitly divides events by everyone for risk and by non-events for odds. Independent calculations give RR 2 and OR 8/3, while the retained adverse-event exercise gives RR 2 and OR 9/4. The full retained teaching preserves rare-event approximation, sampling and noncollapsibility boundaries and rejects an OR as a direct risk multiplier or causal clinical benefit. Both themes make the denominator comparison visible; the full frozen count/denominator task is met.
